prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: side impact at intersection in League City, Texas. Injury: wrist fracture. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1463; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, if that's all right. You can use the placeholder Plaintiff.

Q: We can use a placeholder for the transcript, but I need you to confirm you understand you're under oath today.

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Thank you. Let's talk about the collision. Where were you when it happened?

A: I was driving through an intersection in League City, Texas, heading east. I had a green light.

Q: Were you familiar with that intersection?

A: Yes, I drive through it most weekdays on the way to work.

Q: What happened as you entered the intersection?

A: A vehicle coming from the north ran its red light and struck the driver's side of my car. The impact was on my door, right where I was sitting. I remember the airbag going off and the car spinning a bit before it stopped.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?

A: Only for a second. I saw it coming, but there wasn't time to do anything. I tried to brake, but it was too late.

Q: What did you do with your hands during the impact?

A: I had my right hand on the steering wheel and my left arm braced against the door. When the car spun, my wrist hit the console and the door frame. That's when I felt the pain.

Q: When did you first seek medical care?

A: A paramedic came to the scene, and then I went by ambulance to the emergency room that same day. They took X-rays and told me my wrist was fractured.

Q: What treatment have you received since?

A: They put my wrist in a splint first. Later I had a follow-up with an orthopedic doctor, who recommended a cast for several weeks and then physical therapy. I still go to therapy twice a week.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?

A: It's been hard. I'm right-handed, so simple things like buttoning a shirt, cooking, and typing at work have been difficult. I had to ask my partner to help with grocery bags and driving for a while because I couldn't grip the wheel comfortably.

Q: Have you missed any work?

A: Yes, I was out for several weeks at first. I've since returned on a modified schedule, and I still have some days when my wrist swells and I need to rest it.

Q: Before this accident, did you have any prior injuries to that wrist or arm?

A: No, I had no problems with that wrist before this happened.
